items.title: Two permutations with equal characteristic value admit representatives meeting exactly in the certificates
items.author: Gilad Chase; Neta Dafni; Yuval Filmus; Nathan Lindzey
items.work: Uniqueness for 2-Intersecting Families of Permutations and Perfect Matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 242-244: for a 2-intersecting family of permutations whose common certificate size is at most n minus two, two members with equal characteristic value admit representatives whose certificates meet exactly in the intersection of the original certificates. The proof (source lines 245-257) proves the stronger statement about the intersection rather than merely about the characteristic values, and its heart is a pairing argument: after listing the pairs of the first certificate, the remaining indices are paired cyclically in an order chosen so that none of the new pairs meets the second certificate, which is exactly where the bound on the common certificate size is consumed; the same construction is then run with the certificates exchanged. The statement records only the existence of the representatives.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line
